name: application-tab-overflow-scroller
title: Tab Overflow Scroller
description: Horizontally scrollable tab strip for a fixed set of tabs too wide to fit at once — an arrow-button variant and an edge-fade variant, distinct from application-tabs which assumes all tabs fit in the available width.
useWhen: A fixed set of tab labels is too wide to fit in the available width, especially on narrow screens.
You want explicit prev/next controls for scrolling through tabs, in addition to touch/trackpad scrolling.
A subtle edge-fade hint is enough to signal more tabs exist off-screen, without extra buttons.
avoidWhen: All tabs comfortably fit in the available width — use application-tabs instead, it is simpler.
The tabs need to collapse extras into an overflow menu rather than scroll — a different "+N more" pattern is more appropriate.
Only two or three tabs exist — scrolling affordances add unnecessary complexity for content that always fits.
responsiveBehavior: The tab strip scrolls horizontally within its own overflow-x-auto container at any width; the arrow-button variant keeps its buttons visible while the edge-fade variant relies on the fade cue alone.
accessibility: The scrollable strip carries role='tablist' with each tab as a role='tab' and aria-selected reflecting the active tab.
Arrow buttons in variant 1 carry real aria-labels ('Scroll tabs left/right') since they have no visible text.
The edge-fade overlay in variant 2 is decorative (aria-hidden, pointer-events-none) and does not block interaction with the tabs beneath it.

variants.title: With arrow buttons
variants.description: Scrollable tab strip with prev/next arrow buttons at both ends for explicit scroll control.
accessibility: Both arrow buttons carry a descriptive aria-label since they contain only an icon.

variants.title: With arrow buttons (Dark)
variants.description: Arrow-button scrollable tab strip adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Arrow icon and active-tab underline contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: With edge fade
variants.description: Scrollable tab strip with a subtle edge-fade gradient hinting at more tabs off-screen, relying on native scroll instead of arrow buttons.
accessibility: The fade overlay does not block pointer or keyboard interaction with the tabs underneath it.

variants.title: With edge fade (Dark)
variants.description: Edge-fade scrollable tab strip adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: The fade gradient uses the dark background color so it blends rather than showing a visible seam.
